chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"A man does not take back what he gives to his wife, nor a woman what she gives to her husband, whether he has taken possession of it or not.
Is it not that Allah says, 'That you take back from what you gave them something?' (Quran 2:229)
And He said, 'But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it in satisfaction and ease.' (Quran 4:4)
And this applies to both the dowry (sadaq) and the gift (hiba).
ai.seo_question: Can a husband take back a gift he gave to his wife in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes that gifts between spouses are irrevocable, whether or not possession has been taken, drawing a parallel to the Quranic principle of not reclaiming what has been given. This ruling extends the permissibility of retaining gifts to both the dowry (sadaq) and general gifts (hiba), emphasizing the mutual consent and ease (haneen marieen) highlighted in the verses. The narration underscores the stability of marital financial exchanges in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing them from the revocable gifts of other parties.
